claims.text: Controlled boron microalloying of laser-clad AlCoCrFeNiMoTi coatings induces in situ formation of a fine TiB2 particle dispersion.
Controlled boron microalloying refines the dual-phase microstructure of AlCoCrFeNiMoTi coatings.
The TiB2 dispersion and refined dual-phase microstructure reinforce a self-healing passive oxide film.
The TiB2 dispersion and refined dual-phase microstructure increase coating hardness.
The combined effects on passive-film behavior and hardness govern resistance to simultaneous wear and corrosion.
A refined matrix interspersed with TiB2 particles facilitates formation and maintenance of a continuous passive oxide film.
Boron microalloying introduces local lattice distortions.
Boron-induced lattice distortions refine the coating microstructure.
Boron addition promotes selective TiB2 precipitation during laser cladding.
The resulting dual-phase structure increases microhardness.
Increased microhardness improves resistance to abrasive wear.
The refined phases enhance oxygen diffusion.
Enhanced oxygen diffusion supports rapid repassivation of freshly exposed surfaces.
Rapid repassivation mitigates corrosion during simultaneous mechanical loading.
Optimally boron-doped coatings will have lower wear rates than undoped coatings under the specified test conditions.
Optimally boron-doped coatings will retain adhesion better than undoped coatings.
Optimally boron-doped coatings will maintain a more stable corrosion potential than undoped coatings because of efficient passive-film reformation.
Excessive boron addition will compromise performance by disrupting passive-film continuity.
The predicted improvements are expected during reciprocating sliding in 3.5 wt.% NaCl at approximately 300 °C.
The proposed mechanism may fail when boron content deviates markedly from the optimized range or outside the specified environment.
